subject: english
question:
**Choose the correct meaning of the given idiom.**

Go through fire and water

options.text: To pass through all types of hardships
To pass through all types of luxury
To fail in all types of hardships

solution:
The correct answer is "**To pass through all types of hardships."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An idiom is a group of words, or in other words, a phrase that has a meaning different from the literal meaning of the words in it. 
 
 
• Example: "Under the weather" means feeling ill or getting a cold.
 
 
 
• **The idiom 'go through fire and water' means to face and overcome all types of hardships or difficulties.**
 
• सभी प्रकार की कठिनाइयों या कठिनाइयों का सामना करना और उनसे पार पाना |
 
• The phrase is often used to describe someone who has gone through a lot of challenges and struggles but has come out stronger on the other side.
 
 
• Example: I will go through fire and water for you. 
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: 'To pass through life'** is not the correct meaning of the idiom. It is a literal interpretation that does not capture the figurative sense of the phrase.
 
• **Option 3: 'To pass through all types of luxury'** is the opposite of the intended meaning of the idiom. The phrase is about overcoming hardships, not enjoying luxury.
 
• **Option 4: 'To fail in all types of hardships'** is also the opposite of the intended meaning. The idiom is about overcoming challenges, not succumbing to them.
